definitions.definition: Saṃvara is the stopping of inflow (9.1). Its means are the guptis, samitis, dharma, anuprekṣās, conquest of the parīṣahas and cāritra (9.2); tapas also brings shedding (9.3).

name: The three controls and five carefulnesses

definitions.definition: Gupti is the proper restraint of activity (9.4); the five samitis are īryā, bhāṣā, eṣaṇā, ādāna-nikṣepa, utsarga (9.5).
Supreme forbearance, gentleness, straightforwardness, purity, truth, restraint, austerity, giving up, non-possession and celibacy (9.6).
Repeated contemplation of impermanence, no refuge, saṃsāra, aloneness, otherness, impurity, inflow, stopping, shedding, the universe, rarity of enlightenment and the well-taught dharma (9.7).

Summary only (restricted topic): hardships met on the path that are to be endured, so as not to fall from the path and for shedding (9.8); the sūtras 9.9-9.17 list them, assign them to stages and karma types, and say how many can occur together; none of that detail is reproduced here.

Summary only for the six outer austerities (restricted topic, 9.19). The six inner ones are expiation, reverence, service, study, abandonment and meditation (9.20), with nine, four, ten, five and two kinds for the first five (9.21-9.26).

Dhyāna (9.27) is ārta, raudra, dharmya or śukla (9.28); the last two are causes of liberation (9.29). Ārta: 9.30-9.34. Raudra: 9.35. Dharmya: 9.36. Śukla: four kinds, two for the pūrva-knower and two for the kevalin (9.37-9.44).
Through tapas there is shedding (9.3); at ten stages, from right view to the jina, shedding grows innumerable-fold in order (9.45).

name: The five kinds of unattached ascetic

definitions.definition: Pulāka, vakuśa, kuśīla, nirgrantha and snātaka (9.46), to be set out by restraint, scripture, transgression, tīrtha, mark, leśyā, rebirth and level (9.47).
Kevala arises from the destruction of delusion, and of the obscurations of knowledge and perception and the obstructive karma (10.1).
Complete release from karma through the absence of the causes of bondage and through shedding (10.2); the states cease except perfect right view, knowledge, perception and siddhatva (10.3-10.4).

After release the soul goes upward to the end of the universe (10.5), for four causes (10.6) illustrated by four similes (10.7), and stops for want of the medium of motion (10.8); the liberated are set out under twelve heads (10.9).

name: The four causes of the liberated soul's ascent

definitions.definition: Former impulse, absence of attachment, cutting of the bond and the nature of such motion (10.6), with four similes: the spun potter's wheel, the freed gourd, the castor seed, the flame (10.7).

name: The five states of the soul (Tattvārtha 2.1-2.7)

definitions.definition: The soul's states are aupaśamika, kṣāyika, mixed, audayika and pāriṇāmika (2.1); jīvatva, bhavyatva and abhavyatva are named at 2.7.

name: The triple mark of the existent

definitions.definition: The existent is joined with origination, cessation and persistence (5.30).
